# Charge & Chew

> A free map of every public DC fast charger in the US and the restaurants and stores within a
> 10-minute walk of each one, so an EV driver can plan a charging stop around a meal. On the web
> at https://chargeandchew.com/ and as an iPhone app. No account, no ads.

Data as of November 11, 2026, refreshed weekly: 13,926 DC fast-charger sites, 10,797 of them
with somewhere to eat within a 10-minute walk, matched against 90 restaurant and store chains.

## What the app does

- Search a chain ("IHOP"), a town, a kind of shop ("ice cream") or a whole drive ("LA to Las Vegas with In-N-Out"); the map lists the fast chargers with that place within a walk, shortest walk first.
- Plan a drive: the chargers along the route in driving order, the meal stops that fall at mealtimes in local time, and the longest stretch with no fast charger. It is a driver's plan, not a charging plan: it does not model battery charge.
- Set your car to see which stops your plug fits and a rough 10-80% charge time.
- iPhone app: the same map, plus a home-screen widget for the nearest stop with food and Siri shortcuts.

## Key pages

- [Road Food Index](https://chargeandchew.com/road-food-index/): which chains, interstates and states are best for food at US fast chargers, and the longest charger gaps on popular drives; CSV downloads and a citation line
- [Road trip guides](https://chargeandchew.com/trip/): 152 US drives, each with a meal-timed plan for leaving at 8 am, every fast charger within 5 miles of the route and the food a walk from each
- [City guides](https://chargeandchew.com/in/): the fast chargers with food a walk away in 106 US cities
- [Chains](https://chargeandchew.com/near/): fast chargers near each of the 90 chains, nationally and by state
- [Interstates](https://chargeandchew.com/along/): the fast chargers along major interstates, in route order
- [Support](https://chargeandchew.com/support/): how to use the app, what the numbers mean, how to report a problem
- [Privacy](https://chargeandchew.com/privacy/): what the app does with your data

## Data and its limits

- Chargers: US Department of Energy / NREL Alternative Fuels Data Center (https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/electricity-locations), all networks; under 24 kW, private and truck-only sites left out.
- Restaurants and stores: OpenStreetMap (https://www.openstreetmap.org), © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
- "Within a walk" is within 800 m in a straight line, about 10 minutes at 3 mph; walk times are minimums.
- No live availability, prices or wait times: check the network's own app before relying on a stop.

## Privacy

No account and no sign-in. Location is used on the device to centre the map and is never sent to Charge & Chew. Saved stops and settings stay in the browser or the app. Page views are counted anonymously (GoatCounter, no cookies).

## Findings from the Road Food Index (November 11, 2026)

- 77.5% of US DC fast-charger sites (10,797 of 13,926) have somewhere to eat within a 10-minute walk.
- McDonald's is within a 10-minute walk of more fast chargers than any other restaurant chain: 4,649 sites, 33.4% of all of them, just ahead of Starbucks (4,552).
- Of the restaurant chains, In-N-Out has a fast charger within a walk of the most of its locations: 52.9% of 431. Among all chains it is Flying J, at 75.7% of 218.
- I-5 is the best interstate for food at a fast charger: 90.4% of its chargers have somewhere to eat within a walk. I-91 is the worst, at 63.6%.
- On the 152 drives we plan, the longest stretch with no DC fast charger within 5 miles of the road is 144 miles, between Lusk, WY and Rapid City, SD (Denver to Rapid City).

Cite as: Charge & Chew, "The Road Food Index," data as of November 11, 2026, https://chargeandchew.com/road-food-index/.
